title: Product classes are independent of the computing pairing
statement: Let X be a scheme, F,G module sheaves, D,E two computing tensor resolution pairings [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data], and p,q natural numbers. Let a,b,c be global cocycles in degrees p,q,p+q for the left, right and target resolutions of D, and a-prime,b-prime,c-prime the corresponding cocycles for E. Assume that the transported left classes agree, that the transported right classes agree, and that c and c-prime have underlying sections equal to the sectionwise pairs of their respective input cocycles. Then the transported classes of c and c-prime in H^(p+q)(X,F tensor G) are equal. No bilinear product on cohomology is assumed or asserted.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Section 20.31; Lemma 20.31.3 and the flasque-resolution proof of Lemma 20.31.4 (Tag 0FKV)

proof.text: Sheafify the sectionwise bilinear pairings by the tensor universal property. Leibniz supplies a map from the signed total tensor of the two resolution complexes to the target complex. Precompose with the canonical map from derived tensor to naive tensor and identify the three resolution complexes using their augmentations. For either D or E this gives a derived sheaf map F tensor-derived G to F tensor G.

The derived tensor of degree-zero F and G lies in nonpositive degrees by moduleCup_derived_tensor_connectivity. Apply the upstream proved DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor_map_bijective_of_isLE_of_isGE at n=0, with the source IsLE 0 and the degree-zero target IsGE 0: it identifies these derived morphisms with their H-zero maps directly, without a new truncation theorem. Use moduleCup_canonical_hzero_identification: the canonical derived-to-ordinary map, explicitly transported through any nonpositive K-flat model by the localized p tensor identity, its flat-model isomorphism and Q of the tensor augmentation, is invertible on H-zero. The model calculation is moduleCup_hzero_identification. Under this fixed canonical comparison augmentation_pair forces both D and E to induce the identity on the ordinary tensor. Their derived maps therefore agree.

Apply derived global sections and the naive/derived tensor compatibility diagram of Stacks Lemma 20.31.3 for the map to the one-point ringed space. Its maps on the three computing complexes agree with the canonical class maps because all comparisons extend the augmentations. Taking cohomology shows that the class of the paired cocycle depends only on the two transported input classes, proving the claimed equality even across D and E.

lean.statement:
theorem moduleCup_resolution_invariance {X : Scheme.{uM}} {F G : X.Modules}
    (D E : CupResolutionPairing F G) (p q : ℕ)
    (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.left.K).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (b : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.right.K).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (c : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.target.K).sc (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (a' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.left.K).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (b' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.right.K).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (c' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.target.K).sc (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (ha : D.left.class p a = E.left.class p a')
    (hb : D.right.class q b = E.right.class q b')
    (hc : c.val = D.pair p q ⊤ a.val b.val)
    (hc' : c'.val = E.pair p q ⊤ a'.val b'.val) :
    D.target.class (p + q) c = E.target.class (p + q) c'
